general_information.Description: This course explains the general principles of how wireless systems work, how mobility is supported, what the underlying infrastructure is and what interactions are needed among different functional components. This course focuses on qualitative descriptions and the realistic explanations of relationships between wireless systems and performance parameters. Rather than offering a thorough history behind the development of wireless technologies or an exhaustive list of work being carried out, the course helps students learn this exciting technology through relevant examples such as understanding how a cell phone starts working as soon as they get out of an airplane.
general_information.StudentTasks: - Student is responsible to do all exercises and practical given by instructor in class or at home and submit on time. Do quizzzes each lesson as well as midterm test to get progress marks. - Constantly follow announcements on intranet/CMS at http://cms.fpt.edu.vn for up-to-date course information.

assessments.Knowledge and Skill: - Do simulation to meet experiment objectives and instructor's requirements OR - Do experiment parts in chapter 3 till chapter 15 (Some chapters have 2 or more experiments)
assessments.Grading Guide: - Experiment names should be given at the beginning of the course. - Every group of 3 are assigned with one experiment. - Reports should be contain brief background, experimental objectives, experimental environment, experimental steps, observation, final results, analysis and conclusion (as well as coding program if it is required) - Write programs and do simulation using MATLAB to prove scenarios: 1. Effects of path loss, transmitted frequency, antenna length, small-scale and large-scale fading on receiving signal power 2. Effect of ISI on BER 3. Encoding and Decoding give better BER and compare Convolutional code, Turbo codes and LDPC codes 3. Show diversity gain when sectorizing cells and calculate cell sizes based on link budgets 4. Do calculating bandwidth and trade-off between bandwidth and SNR 5. Dynamic chanel allocation (DCA) is more effective because it can take full advantage of radio resources 6. Handover help improve BER (7. Advanced topics: Simulate a physical layer of GSM/CDMA) 8. Using SimEvents of MATLAB to simulate protocols of wireless sensor networks: LEACH,SEP,ESEP 9. Simulate IEEE 802.11a WLAN Physical Layer 10. TR-UWB (Transmitted Reference Ultra-Wideband) Wireless Communications System OR - Can be assigned one of experiments listed at the end of every chapter in the text book.
assessments.Note: - 20% of total progress mark - Reports must be submitted before slot 26 - Presentation is required for every group. (20 mins per group)

assessments.Grading Guide: - Topics should be given at the beginning of the course. - Groups of 2 are assigned with different topics for preparation and presentation - Each topic should be done with the theory comprehesion and proved by real examples containing images, software, tools and systems…...
assessments.Note: - Presentation: 10 mins per group - Reports are not compulsory - PPT slides of a text book can be used - Additional documents from other sources are encouraged for proving theory comprehension
